mcat_description.short: Prefabricated shelters are factory-manufactured, modular structures assembled on-site from pre-engineered panels or frames — supplied as portable cabins, insulated rooms, or semi-permanent buildings for industrial, defence, telecom, railway, and labour accommodation use.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated shelters are complete, ready-to-install building units manufactured off-site using structural steel frames, PUF (polyurethane foam) sandwich panels, FRP (fibre-reinforced plastic) panels, or mild steel sheet cladding, then transported and erected at the deployment site. They are designed to meet IS:875 load standards and IS:1893 seismic zone requirements, with options for thermal insulation, fire resistance (IS:8183), and IP54-rated weatherproofing for sensitive equipment enclosures. In the Indian B2B market, they serve a wide range of applications — from telecom BTS shelters and railway signalling huts to defence barracks, disaster relief units, labour camps, and portable site offices — with sizes ranging from small security cabins to multi-storey modular structures. Buyers specify shelters by wall panel material, insulation type, floor area, structural load rating, and application-specific features such as HVAC provisions, smoke detectors, and electrical fitouts.

market_context: Prefabricated shelters in India span a wide commercial spectrum — from small FRP/PUF security cabins and telecom BTS enclosures to large multi-storey defence barracks and labour camp complexes. The dominant construction materials in the Indian market are PUF (polyurethane foam) sandwich panels, FRP (fibre-reinforced plastic) panels, and mild steel/galvanised steel frames, with PUF panels being the most widely specified for insulated applications such as telecom and defence shelters. Structural design must comply with IS:875 (load design) and IS:1893 (seismic zone requirements), and insulation panels are governed by IS:8183:1993 for fire and density standards. Key buyer segments include telecom operators (BTS shelters), Indian Railways (signalling huts, passenger shelters), defence establishments (barracks, equipment rooms), and infrastructure contractors (site offices, labour camps). The market is highly customisation-driven — buyers specify dimensions, panel thickness, insulation grade, floor type, electrical fitout, and environmental protection rating (IP54 is a common benchmark for equipment shelters). Manufacturers are concentrated in NCR (Delhi/Noida/Gurugram), Kolkata, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, and Chennai. The keyword signal for 'bike shelter cover' (highest Google impression volume) indicates a secondary consumer/outdoor sub-segment, but this is not the dominant commercial form. Government procurement (defence, railways, PSUs) is a significant demand driver, with MHA and defence tenders specifying detailed technical standards including seismic zone V compliance and mineral/rock wool insulation density of 80 kg/cum.
